current_activity: division attacks along the crests of the Lower Vosges, supplied by pack mules, in the VI Corps attack
notes: Event date: 15 March 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 12 p. 254: on the corps left wing the 42d Infantry Division, attacking along the spine of the Lower Vosges, avoided the roads and villages and followed the crests; pack mules supplied the troops; the CMH table lists the command post at Wimmenau on 15 March). Event definition: the division attacks with VI Corps in the opening of the Seventh Army's Saar-Palatinate offensive; the row places the headquarters. Relationship: VI Corps unspecified_subordination (from 24 Dec 44 to 24 Mar 45, CMH table); Seventh Army assigned (from 24 Dec 44, CMH table); 6th Army Group assigned (from 24 Dec 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. Location: Wimmenau (CMH ETO-OB command-post list, R522 p. 167: listed 15 March 1945); the town centre stands for the command post. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Wimmenau. Event support: moderate (Green Book and CMH list agree on the day). Location support: moderate (command post listed on the date).

current_activity: a regiment of the division cuts the secondary road through the Pfälzer Forest after the German withdrawal
notes: Event date: 22 March 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 12 p. 263: soon after dawn on 22 March a regiment of the 42d Division cut the secondary highway through the Pfaelzer Forest; the division had launched a full-scale assault on the West Wall late on the 21st and had struck a vacuum). current_activity: contingents of the division, with the 45th, overpower some 300 SS guards and liberate the Dachau concentration camp
notes: Event date: 29 April 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 436: en route to Munich contingents of the 42d and 45th Divisions overpowered some 300 SS guards and "unveiled another of Germany's most notorious concentration camps, Dachau"; the passage gives no day; Wikipedia, Dachau concentration camp: the main camp was liberated by US forces on 29 April 1945). Event definition: the division reaches the camp northwest of Munich; the row records the division's position and not the camp's history. Relationship: XV Corps unspecified_subordination (from 19 Apr 45, CMH table); Seventh Army assigned (from 24 Dec 44, CMH table); 6th Army Group assigned (from 24 Dec 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. Location: the Dachau camp, on the northeast edge of the town of Dachau. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Dachau concentration camp. Event support: moderate (the Green Book names the divisions and the camp but not the day; the day is Wikipedia's). Location support: moderate (named place; the camp is a distinct site from the town centre).
